editorial:
Imagine living in a nice, quiet neighborhood where everything looks perfect from the outside. That is where you meet Gerald, a guy who seems totally normal but is actually falling apart inside. After a bad car accident and a messy breakup with his wife, he just snaps. Instead of getting help, he decides to do something crazy. He locks himself inside his house and vows never to leave. He treats his home like a private island, trying to survive on whatever food he can find in the kitchen and closets. It starts off feeling like a weird social project, but it quickly turns into a scary look at how a man loses his mind when he cuts off the rest of the world.

You will really notice how the house starts to feel like a character itself as Gerald gets more unstable. The acting is solid, and it is interesting to see how he tries to justify his madness to himself. While the pace is a bit slow at times, the tension builds up in a way that keeps you guessing. If you like stories about people losing their grip on reality, you should check this out.
endingExplained: In the end, Gerald completely loses touch with what is real. He stops caring about the outside world and the divorce. He becomes obsessed with the idea that his house is the only place that matters. He ends up trapped by his own rules, physically and mentally. The movie wraps up by showing that his attempt to find peace through isolation actually turned his home into a prison that he can no longer escape.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about people losing their minds in isolation.
